cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women with thalassemia minor and 100 non-carrier control pregnant women from a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Thalassemia minor is associated with a significantly higher prevalence of anaemia, increased risk of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), and more frequent low birth weight (LBW) in neonates.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates were significantly higher in thalassemia carriers (42% vs. 30%, p = 0.040) compared to non-carriers.
